title: Epochal benchmark orchestrator for CI smoke & regression checks
creator: Marcus Nguyen
description:
Problem: PRs and rolling commits occasionally introduce subtle performance regressions that show up as increases in p95 or drops in tokens/sec. Existing CI baseline runs are heavyweight and often miss regressions that only appear after KV-cache priming or with representative prompt mixes. Goal: ship a lightweight, deterministic orchestrator that runs an epochal smoke benchmark on PRs and scheduled commits, produces stable baselines, and gates merges when a high-confidence regression is detected.

Approach: build a modular 'epochal benchmark orchestrator' service that coordinates: (1) stratified synthetic workload generator (short/medium/long contexts, diverse prompt shapes and model variants), (2) ephemeral harness VMs/GPU tasks with controlled warmup and KV-cache priming, (3) rolling baseline storage with metadata (model revision, hardware, kernel profile), (4) statistical decision layer combining t-tests, bootstrap CI, and a lightweight Bayesian change detector to provide a regression confidence score, and (5) CI integration that posts GitHub check results with artifacts + rerun hooks. Key heuristics: adaptive thresholds based on historical variance, require min sample size and warmed KV states before measurement, separate throughput (tokens/sec) vs latency (p95) pass criteria, and use ensemble-signal fusion to reduce false positives.

Operational notes: results must include raw traces, aggregated histograms, and a deterministic artifact (bench artifact id) stored in S3. Provide a human-friendly dashboard view in Console for triage and a runbook for owners to triage blocked PRs. The orchestrator will be configured to run as a fast smoke check on PRs (short sample, strict gating) and as an extended nightly job (larger sample, automatic baseline refresh).
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator service can run a deterministic smoke benchmark on a PR and produce a bench artifact ID
GitHub PR check posts pass/fail with a regression confidence score and links to artifacts
Baseline storage supports rolling baselines per (model, commit range, hardware profile) and can be queried by bench artifact ID
Regression detection uses at least two statistical methods (Welch t-test + bootstrap) and returns a combined confidence score
Dashboard in Console shows p95 and tokens/sec deltas against baseline and links to raw traces
Runbook for on-call outlining triage, reruns, and temporary bypass policy is published
progress_updates: 2026-02-16 - Marcus Nguyen: Spike completed for stratified workload generator. Found that short-context mixes expose throughput regressions earlier than long-context mixes.
2026-02-22 - Aisha Patel: Prototype harness implemented; uses a 3-stage warmup (cold, kv-prime, steady) and uploads artifacts to s3://redwood-ci/bench-artifacts/epochal/
2026-02-28 - Aisha Patel: Initial Bayesian change detector integrated; observed two false positives from noisy infra; added adaptive variance floor and minimum sample policy.
2026-03-04 - Samir Rao (review): Suggested adding a paired-sample bootstrap for p95 comparison when same requests are replayed under two commits to reduce variance.
2026-03-08 - Aisha Patel: Integrated GitHub Checks API to post summary and artifact links; implemented rerun button that triggers full harness with expanded sample size for confirmation.
2026-03-10 - Marcus Nguyen: End-to-end test on a synthetic regression introduced a 12% tokens/sec drop; orchestrator flagged with 96% confidence and blocked merge as expected.
notes: Trade-offs: stricter PR gating reduces noise but increases flake risk; mitigations include a rerun-with-expanded-sample CI action and a short 'manual override' flow for urgent patches.
We intentionally separate throughput and latency checks so teams can opt into gating on one or both metrics depending on customer impact.
Future: add lightweight shadow traffic tests against dedicated pools to catch regressions that only appear under realistic multiplexing patterns.
